done_when: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test proves, so a proof list never names a test that did not run

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. A second `forge close` on an unchanged branch replaces the pull request’s test results with preliminary proof text. This line rebuilds evidence without a run report; the fresh-review path at `close.py:321-323` skips the cached passing test run, then publishes that preliminary evidence. The command test covers the first close only.
findings.title: Not done: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test גves

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. New evidence beyond the earlier JavaScript finding: Forge documents Jest selection including `__tests__` files (`src/forge/templates/skill.md:1123-1124`), but `TEST_NAME` does not recognize a path such as `__tests__/greeting.js`. When the worker names that file, `names` is empty and this branch copies the line unchanged into the final pull request, even if the test did not run. It is not marked `not checked` as the recorded narrow rule requires.
findings.title: Close copies Jest __tests__ filenames without checking them

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 1-2, reversible; third finding in review.py, so one general rule instead of per-language cases): any proof line naming a test that close cannot match to its own run's results, in any language, is published as not checked; reading JavaScript runners' per-test results is a follow-up. The failed-test case gets its assertion this round.

why: Workers write proof lists by hand, and about one review round in five is a gate on a missing or wrong test name in that list
